1.title: Management Practices and Practice Guides
1.text: Welcome to Module ten: Management Practices and Practice Guides. It covers the exam area The eye til Value System. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. Define management practice. Know the two practice groups (general, and product and service management). Understand the role of the practices within the eye til Value System. Explain the structure and the benefits of the eye til Practice Guides. Define metric and critical success factor. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: The eye til Value System (forty percent). Exam format: forty multiple-choice questions in sixty minutes; twenty-six correct answers (sixty-five percent) pass. Validated against: the official eye til Foundation (Version five) syllabus, version five point zero (February two thousand twenty-six).

1.title: What a management practice is
1.text: What a management practice is. A management practice is a set of organizational resources designed for performing work or accomplishing an objective. It combines people, processes, information and technology, and partners (the four dimensions). eye til describes thirty-four management practices. They are organized into two groups. General management practices. What it covers: Practices adopted from general business and used across the organization. Examples: strategy management, risk management, information security management. Product and service management practices. What it covers: Practices developed for product and service management. Examples: incident management, problem management, change enablement, service desk.

1.title: What a management practice is, continued
1.text: What a management practice is. The figure shows this: Two groups of management practices inside the eye til Value System.

1.title: What a management practice is, continued
1.text: What a management practice is. eye til four had three groups: general, service and technical management practices. Version five uses two. Exam tip: Two groups: general, and product and service. If an option lists "general, service and technical", it is the old wording.

1.title: Role of the practices in the Value System
1.text: Role of the practices in the Value System. The practices are the third working element the value chain activities draw on: each activity uses one or more practices, and a practice can contribute to several activities. The practices turn guiding principles and governance into repeatable work.

1.title: The ITIL Practice Guides
1.text: The eye til Practice Guides. Each practice is described in an eye til Practice Guide that gives practical guidance. Typically a guide covers (in plain words). Purpose and key terms. What the practice is for, and its vocabulary. Scope and value. What it covers, and the value it brings. Processes and activities. The work done inside the practice. Four dimensions. Organizations and people, information and technology, partners and suppliers, value streams. Success factors and metrics. How to tell the practice is working. Benefits: the guides give a consistent structure, reusable good practice, and a common language across teams.

1.title: Metric and critical success factor
1.text: Metric and critical success factor. Metric. A measurement or calculation that is monitored and reported to show how well something performs. Critical success factor (C S F). A necessary precondition for success: something that must happen for an outcome to be achieved. Exam tip: A C S F (critical success factor) says what must be true. A metric says how you measure it. Exam tip: Two groups in Version five: general and product and service management. An option with three groups (general, service, technical) is the eye til four wording.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Which statement about management practices in Version five is C O R R E C T? (one) They are organized into two groups. (two) One group is general management practices. (three) They are organized into general, service and technical groups. (four) There are only five of them. The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: one and two. Two groups, one of which is general.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Incident management belongs to which practice group? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Product and service management practices. Incident management is developed for product and service management.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A team asks which target must be true for a project to succeed. Which term describes it? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Critical success factor. A C S F is a necessary precondition for success.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Identify the missing word(s). A blank is a set of organizational resources designed for performing work or accomplishing an objective. The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Management practice. That is the definition of a management practice.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. What is the main benefit of the eye til Practice Guides? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: They give a consistent, practical structure for each practice. They offer consistent, reusable guidance.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A manager reports the percentage of incidents resolved within the agreed time. What is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A metric. A measurement monitored and reported is a metric.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Define a management practice. Answer: A set of organizational resources designed for performing work or accomplishing an objective. Question two. How many practice groups are there in Version five? Answer: Two. Question three. Name them. Answer: General management practices, and product and service management practices.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. How many practices does eye til describe? Answer: thirty-four. Question five. Define a critical success factor. Answer: A necessary precondition for success. Question six. What is a metric? Answer: A measurement or calculation that is monitored and reported.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Management practice: resources designed for performing work or reaching an objective. Groups: general; product and service management. Practice Guide: purpose, scope, processes, four dimensions, success factors and metrics. C S F or metric: must be true or how it is measured. Old wording: general, service, technical.
